A build that fetches and parses for minutes under any traffic changes a size or a modification time there, so the check refuses a clean build. Exempting those stores blinds the check exactly where a tool would do harm. The plan also hands the tool the live CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR, and every one of those modules writes under it, so a build tool that imports concordance code writes into the live stores by default. A quiet stand-in shows none of this. To answer: confine or attribute the tool's own writes instead of diffing the shared tree. For example, point CONCORDANCE_DATA_DIR, every CONCORDANCE_*_DIR, HOME, TMPDIR and the working directory under its temporary directory, name any read-only inputs it needs, and refuse any write it makes outside that directory. TESTS: the stand-in as written neither keeps the tests off the box nor runs the real script inside its temporary directory. (a) tools/deploy.sh:171 runs tools/verify_deploy.py after every deploy that passes its gates, and that file holds its own host, key and destination (verify_deploy.py:49-51), which the plan does not make overridable. ORDER: the temporary directory sits 'beside its output directory', and nothing says it is removed when the tool fails, leaves it empty or trips the isolation check. THE UNIT, tools/box_build.py build <name>, runs on the box under a lock held only by builds, one the kernel releases if the process dies (a second build is refused, and writes its refusal only to its own run id's result file).
